## createRemoteClient() function

Create a client for one app that runs its operations on a macts service.

**Signature:**

```typescript
declare function createClient<Client, Resources extends ResourceTable>(
  app: AppContract<Client, Resources>,
  options: RemoteClientOptions
): Client & ClientBrand<Resources>
```

**Returns:**

Client &amp; ClientBrand&lt;Resources&gt;

The app's client. Its type also carries the contract's resource table, which `bindReference` reads; the client has no member for it.

## Exceptions

`TypeError` when `url` is not an absolute URL or `token` contains characters that cannot be sent in a header.

## Remarks

The client never loads the app manifest or any Mac-side code; the service holds the manifest and enforces every check. Every method resolves to the operation's SDK result or throws a canonical structured error from `@macts/contracts`<!-- -->, exactly as the local client does. Values are validated on the way out (`ValidationError`<!-- -->, before any request is sent) and on the way back (`UnexpectedValueError`<!-- -->).

## Example

```typescript
import { createClient, resolveClientOptions, TargetNotFoundError } from '@macts/sdk'
import { calendarContract } from '@macts/calendar/contract'

const calendar = createClient(calendarContract, resolveClientOptions())
try {
  await calendar.events.get({ uid: 'missing' })
} catch (error) {
  if (error instanceof TargetNotFoundError) console.log('No such event')
  else throw error
}
```
